lines: The blade did its work, and so did my feet when it was time to come home.
Heat, pressure, <dark_gray><wavy>fear</wavy></dark_gray>. Good steel survives that. So did I.
Steel sang, fear shouted, and I still heard the way home.
I cleaned the weapon before I noticed my hands were shaking.
Retreat was the right choice, even if pride disagreed.
Some wounds only began hurting after the gate closed behind me.
The first quiet moment felt stranger than the fighting.
Tired legs carried me farther than the blade did.
I survived because I knew when steel was not enough.
The sound of the forge told me I was home.
A clean edge cannot replace good judgment.
I remember every strike the weapon caught for me.
The grip is stained, but it never slipped.
I came back with one new scar and several new rules.
The blade needs repair. So do I.
I did not feel brave. I felt busy staying alive.
Fear stayed with me until the hammer started again.
Next time I carry more bandages and less pride.
The fight ended before my hands understood it had.
Survival is not pretty work, but it is honest.
